In [[probability theory]], an '''excursion probability''' is the probability that a [[stochastic process]] surpasses a given value in a fixed time period. It is the probability<ref name="adler">{{Cite book | first1=Robert J. |last1= Adler |first2= Jonathan E. |last2=Taylor| doi = 10.1007/978-0-387-48116-6_4 | chapter = Excursion Probabilities | title = Random Fields and Geometry | url=https://archive.org/details/randomfieldsgeom00adle_474 | url-access=limited | series = Springer Monographs in Mathematics | pages = [https://archive.org/details/randomfieldsgeom00adle_474/page/n88 75]–76 | year = 2007 | isbn = 978-0-387-48112-8 }}</ref>
:<math>\mathbb P \left\{ \sup_{t \in T} f(t) \geq u \right\}.</math>
Numerous approximation methods for the situation where ''u'' is large and f(''t'') is a [[Gaussian process]] have been proposed such as [[Rice's formula]].<ref name="adler" /><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Adler | first1 = R. J. | doi = 10.1214/aoap/1019737664 | title = On excursion sets, tube formulas and maxima of random fields | journal = [[The Annals of Applied Probability]]| volume = 10 | pages = 1 | year = 2000 | jstor = 2667187| doi-access = free }}</ref> First-excursion probabilities can be used to describe deflection to a critical point experienced by structures during "random loadings, such as earthquakes, strong gusts, hurricanes, etc."<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Yang | first1 = J. -N. | title = First-excursion probability in non-stationary random vibration | doi = 10.1016/0022-460X(73)90059-X | journal = [[Journal of Sound and Vibration]]| volume = 27 | issue = 2 | pages = 165–182 | year = 1973 }}</ref>
